added_items.item: Django solution: django-cors-headers with INSTALLED_APPS, MIDDLEWARE placement, and CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
Do not set CORS headers in both the proxy and the app, because duplicate values cause errors
Origin must match exactly: localhost vs 127.0.0.1 are different origins
If preflight OPTIONS returns 404/405, the route or a proxy is blocking it
Explicit list of raw headers to send, as a framework-agnostic option
Step to verify the fix by reloading and checking Network tab for Access-Control-Allow-Origin
Check server logs for crashes hiding behind the CORS error
credentials: true included in the Express and FastAPI examples
Django fix: django-cors-headers, INSTALLED_APPS, middleware placement, CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
Allow-Credentials should be sent only if using cookies; browser rejects it combined with * (Y also covers the * restriction under credentials)
Duplicate CORS headers set in both proxy and app cause errors
Origin must match exactly: localhost vs 127.0.0.1 differ
Verify fix by checking Network tab for Access-Control-Allow-Origin in response
Explicit example headers block including Allow-Credentials and sample values
